points.title: 出身与早年
points.description: 郑和出生于云南昆阳的一个回族家庭，原名马三宝。他的祖父和父亲都曾前往麦加朝圣，这使得郑和从小接触到了伊斯兰文化和航海知识。1371年，明朝军队征服云南，10岁的郑和被俘，随后被阉割送入宫中成为太监。这段经历使郑和失去了正常人的生活，但也为他后来成为航海家奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Zheng He was born in Kunyang, Yunnan to a Hui Muslim family, originally named Sanbao Ma. His grandfather and father had both made pilgrimages to Mecca, exposing young Zheng He to Islamic culture and navigation knowledge. In 1371, when Ming forces conquered Yunnan, the 10-year-old Zheng He was captured, castrated, and sent to the imperial court as a eunuch. This experience deprived him of a normal life but laid the foundation for his later career as a navigator.

points.title: 宫廷生涯
points.description: 郑和进入南京宫廷后，因聪明能干被燕王朱棣赏识，成为其亲信。在靖难之役中，郑和跟随朱棣南征北战，立下战功，逐渐得到提拔。1399年，朱棣被封为燕王，郑和被任命为内官监太监，负责管理宫廷事务。这段宫廷生涯使郑和积累了丰富的政治和军事经验，也培养了他的忠诚和领导才能，为他后来的航海事业奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After entering the Nanjing court, Zheng He was valued by Prince Zhu Di (Yan Wang) for his intelligence and capability, becoming a trusted confidant. During the Jingnan Campaign, Zheng He followed Zhu Di in battles, making military contributions and gradually rising in rank. In 1399, when Zhu Di was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, Zheng He was appointed as a eunuch of the Neiguanjian, responsible for managing court affairs. This court life allowed Zheng He to accumulate rich political and military experience, cultivating his loyalty and leadership skills that laid the foundation for his later maritime career.

points.title: 七下西洋的起点
points.description: 1405年，明成祖朱棣即位后，任命郑和为正使，率领庞大船队首次下西洋。船队从南京出发，在太仓集结后，经由刘家港出海。郑和在此地组建了由62艘宝船和27,000多人组成的庞大舰队，配备了先进的航海技术和丰富的物资。这一阶段，郑和不仅负责船队的组建和训练，还制定了详细的航海计划，收集了大量的地理和天文资料，为后续的远航奠定了坚实基础。南京作为明朝的都城，是郑和七下西洋的总指挥部和物资供应基地。
points.descriptionEn: In 1405, after Emperor Yongle (Zhu Di) ascended the throne, he appointed Zheng He as the chief envoy to lead the first voyage to the Western Oceans. The fleet departed from Nanjing, assembled in Taicang, and then set sail via Liujiagang. Zheng He organized a massive fleet of 62 treasure ships and over 27,000 people, equipped with advanced navigation technology and abundant supplies. During this period, Zheng He was responsible for forming and training the fleet, developing detailed navigation plans, and collecting extensive geographical and astronomical data, laying a solid foundation for subsequent voyages. Nanjing, as the Ming capital, served as the command center and supply base for Zheng He's seven voyages.

points.title: 七下西洋的壮举
points.titleEn: The Seven Voyages to the Western Oceans
points.description: 郑和率领船队七次下西洋，历时28年，访问了30多个国家和地区，最远到达非洲东海岸和红海。在东南亚，郑和船队建立了贸易关系，调解了当地冲突，如暹罗与满剌加的争端。在印度，郑和访问了古里、锡兰等重要港口，促进了文化交流。在阿拉伯地区，郑和与当地统治者建立了友好关系，收集了大量伊斯兰文化资料。在非洲，郑和带回了长颈鹿、斑马等珍奇动物。这些航行不仅展示了明朝的国力，促进了海上丝绸之路的繁荣，也加强了中外文化交流，扩大了中国的影响力。
points.descriptionEn: Zheng He led seven voyages to the Western Oceans over 28 years, visiting more than 30 countries and regions, reaching as far as the east coast of Africa and the Red Sea. In Southeast Asia, his fleet established trade relations and mediated local conflicts, such as disputes between Siam and Malacca. In India, Zheng He visited important ports like Calicut and Ceylon, promoting cultural exchange. In the Arab region, he established friendly relations with local rulers and collected extensive Islamic cultural materials. In Africa, Zheng He brought back exotic animals like giraffes and zebras. These voyages not only demonstrated Ming's power and promoted the prosperity of the Maritime Silk Road but also strengthened cultural exchange and expanded China's influence.

points.title: 逝世与遗产
points.description: 1433年，郑和在第七次下西洋的返航途中，于印度古里（今印度喀拉拉邦科泽科德）病逝，享年62岁。郑和的逝世标志着明朝航海事业的衰落。他的船队将他的遗体带回南京，安葬于牛首山。郑和一生七下西洋，率领当时世界上最庞大的船队，访问了30多个国家和地区，促进了中外贸易和文化交流，展示了明朝的国力和开放态度。他的航海技术和组织能力在当时世界领先，对后世航海事业产生了深远影响。郑和被视为中国古代航海家的杰出代表，也是中外友好交流的象征。
points.descriptionEn: In 1433, during the return journey of his seventh voyage, Zheng He fell ill and died in Calicut (present-day Kozhikode, Kerala, India) at the age of 62. His death marked the decline of Ming maritime endeavors. His fleet brought his body back to Nanjing, where he was buried on Niushou Mountain. Throughout his life, Zheng He led seven voyages, commanding the world's largest fleet of the time, visiting over 30 countries and regions, promoting Sino-foreign trade and cultural exchange, and demonstrating the power and openness of the Ming Dynasty. His navigation technology and organizational skills were world-class at the time, leaving a profound impact on later maritime endeavors. Zheng He is regarded as an outstanding representative of ancient Chinese navigators and a symbol of friendly international exchange.

appraisal.zh: 郑和是15世纪初世界航海史上规模空前的航海家，七下西洋展现明朝国力，船队规模与航程在当时无人能及，以贸易与文化交流为主，促进了亚洲区域内的往来，其记录与地图为后世留下珍贵地理资料。不过也有研究者指出，这些航行耗费巨大而经济收益有限，朝中亦有官员主张将资源转用于北方防务，且郑和身后明朝即行海禁，航海活动缺乏制度支撑而难以为继。
appraisal.en: Zheng He is a navigator of unprecedented scale in early 15th-century maritime history; his seven voyages displayed Ming power, and the size and reach of his fleet were unmatched at the time. Focused on trade and cultural exchange, they promoted interaction within Asia, and his records and maps left valuable geographical material. Yet researchers also note the voyages were enormously costly with limited economic return, some officials favored spending on northern defense, and the maritime ban imposed soon after his death left the enterprise without institutional support.

supporter.zh: 郑和被视为中国古代最伟大的航海家，他的七下西洋壮举展示了明朝的国力和开放胸怀。支持者认为郑和的航海活动促进了中外贸易和文化交流，扩大了中国的影响力，为海上丝绸之路的繁荣做出了巨大贡献。郑和的航海技术和组织能力在当时世界领先，他的船队规模之大、航行范围之广，在15世纪初的世界无人能及。郑和被视为和平外交的典范，他的航海活动以贸易和文化交流为主，而非殖民扩张，体现了中国古代的和平外交理念。
supporter.en: Zheng He is regarded as China's greatest navigator, with his seven voyages demonstrating the power and openness of the Ming Dynasty. Supporters believe his maritime activities promoted Sino-foreign trade and cultural exchange, expanding China's influence and greatly contributing to the prosperity of the Maritime Silk Road. His navigation technology and organizational skills were world-class at the time, with the scale and reach of his fleet unmatched in the early 15th century. Zheng He is seen as a model of peaceful diplomacy, as his voyages focused on trade and cultural exchange rather than colonial expansion, reflecting ancient Chinese diplomatic philosophy.

critic.zh: 批评者认为郑和的航海活动虽然规模宏大，但经济效益有限，消耗了大量国家资源。每次航行耗费巨大，却未能为明朝带来持久的经济利益或战略优势。此外，郑和的航海活动在明朝内部也存在争议，一些官员认为这些航行耗费国力，不如将资源用于北方防御蒙古。批评者还指出，郑和的航海活动未能持续，在他死后不久，明朝便实行海禁政策，关闭了海上丝绸之路，这表明郑和的航海活动缺乏制度性支持，难以持续发展。
critic.en: Critics argue that despite their grand scale, Zheng He's voyages had limited economic returns, consuming vast national resources. Each expedition was extremely costly yet failed to bring sustained economic benefits or strategic advantages to the Ming Dynasty. Additionally, these voyages faced internal opposition, with some officials arguing that the resources would be better spent on defending against Mongol threats in the north. Critics also note that the voyages could not be sustained after Zheng He's death, as the Ming Dynasty soon implemented a maritime ban policy, closing the Maritime Silk Road, indicating a lack of institutional support for continued maritime development.

objective.zh: 从历史学角度看，郑和的航海活动是15世纪初世界航海史上的壮举，代表了当时中国最先进的航海技术和组织能力。在流行文化中，郑和被视为中国古代对外开放的象征，与后来西方的航海探险形成鲜明对比。历史学界普遍认为，郑和的航海活动虽然未能像欧洲大航海那样引发全球性变革，但它们在促进亚洲区域内的文化交流和贸易方面发挥了重要作用。郑和的航海记录和地图也为后世提供了宝贵的地理资料，对中国和世界航海史都具有重要意义。
objective.en: From a historical perspective, Zheng He's voyages were a remarkable achievement in early 15th-century maritime history, representing China's most advanced navigation technology and organizational capabilities at the time. In popular culture, Zheng He is seen as a symbol of ancient China's openness to the outside world, forming a stark contrast to later European maritime explorations. Historians generally agree that while Zheng He's voyages did not trigger global transformations like the European Age of Discovery, they played a significant role in promoting cultural exchange and trade within Asia. Zheng He's navigation records and maps also provided valuable geographical information for later generations, holding important significance for both Chinese and world maritime history.

self.zh: 国家欲富强，不可置海洋于不顾。财富取之海洋，危险亦来自海洋。一旦海禁，将何以富强？
self.en: If a nation wishes to be rich and powerful, it cannot ignore the oceans. Wealth comes from the seas, but so do dangers. Once maritime trade is banned, how can the nation become rich and powerful?
